slides.text: I was stranded in a tiny village in rural Italy, entirely out of my element and unable to speak a single word of the language. Mateo, the brooding, gorgeous son of the local innkeeper, took pity on me. Since we shared no spoken language, we communicated solely through my battered English-Italian pocket dictionary, passing it back and forth under the warm Tuscan sun while he showed me his beautiful hometown.

It was agonizingly slow, but incredibly intimate. We’d sit on the terracotta terrace, our fingers accidentally brushing as we traced words on the thin pages. He'd point to 'beautiful,' looking right into my eyes. I'd frantically flip to 'breathtaking.' I fell devastatingly in love in total silence. But my visa expired, and the yellow cab arrived to take me back to a life that suddenly felt utterly hollow and grey.

As I loaded my suitcase, Mateo rushed out, his chest heaving. He didn't say goodbye. He just pressed the worn dictionary into my chest and walked away. On the plane, crying softly, I opened the book. He had crossed out every single word in the entire dictionary with a heavy black marker, except for three English words that he had circled repeatedly in bright red ink: 'Stay. With. Me.'
